title: Grade 11 Chemistry — Chemical Equilibrium
description: Equilibrium constant, Le Chatelier's principle, acids and bases
subject: chemistry

questions.question: Chemical equilibrium is established when:
options: The rate of forward reaction equals the rate of reverse reaction
questions.explanation: At equilibrium: rate_forward = rate_reverse. Concentrations are constant (not zero). The equilibrium is dynamic — both reactions continue at equal rates.

questions.question: For the reaction aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD, the equilibrium constant Kc is:
questions.explanation: Kc = [C]^c[D]^d / [A]^a[B]^b (Law of Mass Action). Square brackets = molar concentrations at equilibrium. Pure solids and liquids are excluded from Kc expression.

questions.question: If Kc >> 1 (very large), the reaction at equilibrium:
questions.explanation: Kc >> 1: reaction goes nearly to completion — products are heavily favoured. Kc << 1: reactants are favoured (little product formed). Kc ≈ 1: significant amounts of both.

questions.question: Le Chatelier's Principle states that if a system at equilibrium is disturbed:
options: The system shifts to counteract the disturbance and reach a new equilibrium
questions.explanation: Le Chatelier's Principle: a system at equilibrium responds to a disturbance by shifting to OPPOSE the change. Note: changing T changes Kc; changing concentration or pressure shifts equilibrium but Kc stays the same.

questions.question: For N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ (Haber Process), increasing pressure shifts equilibrium:
options: To the left (toward more moles of gas)
To the right (toward fewer moles of gas — 4 moles → 2 moles)
No shift (pressure doesn't affect gas equilibria)
questions.explanation: Increasing pressure favours the side with fewer moles of gas: 4 moles (1N₂ + 3H₂) → 2 moles (2NH₃). Equilibrium shifts right, producing more ammonia. Hence high pressure is used in the Haber Process.

questions.question: Arrhenius definition of an acid is:
options: A substance that produces H⁺ ions in aqueous solution
A substance that reacts with bases
questions.explanation: Arrhenius acid: produces H⁺ (hydrogen ions) in water. Arrhenius base: produces OH⁻. Limited to aqueous solutions. Brønsted-Lowry is broader: acid = proton donor, base = proton acceptor.

questions.question: The pH of a solution with [H⁺] = 10⁻³ mol/L is:
questions.explanation: pH = −log[H⁺] = −log(10⁻³) = 3. pH < 7: acidic. pH = 7: neutral. pH > 7: basic. pOH = 14 − pH = 11.

questions.question: A buffer solution resists changes in pH when:
options: Small amounts of acid or base are added to it
questions.explanation: A buffer resists pH change when small amounts of acid/base are added. A buffer contains: (1) weak acid + its conjugate base (salt), e.g., CH₃COOH + CH₃COONa. Used in biological systems (blood pH 7.4).

questions.question: The reaction quotient Q is used to:
options: Determine which direction a reaction will proceed to reach equilibrium (compare Q to K)
questions.explanation: Q = Kc expression calculated with CURRENT concentrations (not necessarily equilibrium). If Q < K: forward reaction proceeds. Q > K: reverse reaction proceeds. Q = K: at equilibrium.

questions.question: Increasing temperature for an exothermic reaction shifts equilibrium:
options: To the left (reverse reaction favoured — to absorb added heat)
questions.explanation: For exothermic reaction: heat is a product. Adding heat (increasing T) shifts equilibrium LEFT (Le Chatelier). This DECREASES Kc. For endothermic reactions, increasing T shifts right and increases Kc.

questions.question: The solubility product (Ksp) of AgCl is:
questions.explanation: AgCl(s) ⇌ Ag⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq). Ksp = [Ag⁺][Cl⁻]. Pure solid (AgCl) is excluded from expression. If ionic product > Ksp: precipitation occurs. If < Ksp: unsaturated (no precipitate).

questions.question: Adding a catalyst to a reaction at equilibrium:
options: Does not shift equilibrium — speeds up both forward and reverse reactions equally
questions.explanation: A catalyst speeds up BOTH forward AND reverse reactions equally — it does not change the equilibrium position or Kc. It only helps the system REACH equilibrium faster. Industrial importance: Haber process (Fe catalyst).

questions.question: The relationship between Kc and Kp for a gas reaction is: Kp = ?
questions.explanation: Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn where Δn = (moles of gaseous products) − (moles of gaseous reactants). R = 0.0821 L·atm/(mol·K). If Δn = 0: Kp = Kc.

questions.question: Lewis acids are:
options: Electron pair acceptors (can accept electron pairs from Lewis bases)
questions.explanation: Lewis acid: electron pair acceptor (e.g., BF₃, AlCl₃, H⁺, FeCl₃). Lewis base: electron pair donor (e.g., NH₃, H₂O, OH⁻). Lewis concept is the broadest acid-base theory.

questions.question: Common ion effect: adding NaCl to a saturated AgCl solution will:
options: Precipitate more AgCl (decrease solubility — Cl⁻ shifts equilibrium left)
questions.explanation: Common ion effect: adding Cl⁻ (from NaCl) to AgCl(s) ⇌ Ag⁺ + Cl⁻ shifts equilibrium LEFT (Le Chatelier). More AgCl precipitates. Solubility decreases. Ksp is unchanged (only depends on T).
